📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-07-04-crm-amqp-consumer-monitor-family-quiet-period-flap`
This is occurrence #200 (lifetime count). The last post was at 2026-11-22 18:29Z, inside the 24h window, so this one posts only because of the every-10th-occurrence resurface rule.
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `Admin` (`admin` usergroup / `#team-admin`, inert) for method-mobile-notifications-subscriber; DD tags say team:crm
Playbook: confirm the No Data is a quiet-period gap (traffic resumes on its own), confirm 0 `status:error` logs, and treat it as noise. Escalate only if the gap stays open >2h in business hours or a sibling error/latency monitor co-fires.
Open Jira: none

Source alerts (1 total): monitor 302055141 `[CRM] method-mobile-notifications-subscriber heartbeat - consumer silent`. No Data at 04:24:21Z, recovered at 04:55:21Z. This was a degraded cycle (Slack MCP unavailable), so there are no permalinks. The same monitor went No Data again at 07:01:21Z (recovered 07:46:21Z, occ #201, suppressed). Overnight, runtime-core-subscriber 302057011 also flapped 5 times (occ #195-199, all suppressed, 0 errors).

Root-cause analysis:
  • `sum:trace.amqp.command.hits{service:method-mobile-notifications-subscriber,env:prod}.as_rate()` 02:00-08:30Z: sparse points of 0.008-0.075/s, with two gaps: 03:22Z->04:54Z (92 min) and 06:00Z->07:44Z (104 min). Each No Data sits inside a gap, and traffic resumed by itself both times.
  • `service:method-mobile-notifications-subscriber status:error` 03:00-08:00Z: 0 events.
  • Reasoning: at 04:00-07:00Z (overnight US) there are simply no pushes to consume for more than 60 min, which trips the heartbeat's 60-min No Data window. The consumer is idle, not stalled.

Corroborate independently:
  • DD metric: https://app.datadoghq.com/metric/explorer?live=false&page=0&exp_metric=trace.amqp.command.hits&exp_scope=service%3Amethod-mobile-notifications-subscriber%2Cenv%3Aprod&exp_agg=avg&start=1795399200&end=1795422600
  • DD logs (0 errors): https://app.datadoghq.com/logs?query=service%3Amethod-mobile-notifications-subscriber%20status%3Aerror&from_ts=1795402800000&to_ts=1795420800000&live=false
  • DD monitor: https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/302055141

📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-07-07-notifications-p95-latency-monitor-noise`
This is occurrence #52 (lifetime count). The last post was on 2026-11-21 at 09:31Z, more than 24h ago.
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `CRM Experience` (`customer-management` usergroup / `#team-customer-management`, inert)
Playbook: break p95 down by resource. If the spike is only signalr connect/reconnect spans and short requests stay under 1s with 0 errors, it's monitor-scope noise, not user latency.
Open Jira: none

Source alerts (1 total): monitor 302056327 `[CRM][P2] notifications P95 latency high`. It triggered at 09:31:07Z and recovered at 09:41:07Z. This was a degraded cycle, so there are no permalinks.

Root-cause analysis:
  • `p95:trace.aspnet.request{service:notifications,env:prod}` 09:10-09:45Z: 210 points, exactly 1 above 1s, which was 6,780.8s at 09:30:00Z. Everything else was sub-second.
  • By resource at 09:30Z: get_/signalr/reconnect 86,487s and get_/signalr/connect 6,083s (connection lifetimes up to ~24h closing together), negotiate 3.9s, ping/start <0.25s.
  • `service:notifications status:error` 09:10-09:45Z: 0 events.
  • New detail: this fired at the same minute as the previous occurrence (2026-11-21 09:31:07Z). That points to a daily ~09:30Z recycle/restart of notifications that drops every long-held SignalR connection at once. Fix is unchanged: exclude signalr connect/reconnect/poll resources from the monitor's p95.

Corroborate independently:
  • DD metric: https://app.datadoghq.com/metric/explorer?live=false&page=0&exp_metric=trace.aspnet.request.duration.by.resource_service.95p&exp_scope=service%3Anotifications%2Cenv%3Aprod&exp_agg=avg&start=1795425000&end=1795427100
  • DD APM traces: https://app.datadoghq.com/apm/traces?query=service%3Anotifications%20%40duration%3A%3E1s&start=1795425900000&end=1795426500000
  • DD logs (0 errors): https://app.datadoghq.com/logs?query=service%3Anotifications%20status%3Aerror&from_ts=1795425000000&to_ts=1795427100000&live=false
  • DD monitor: https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/302056327
